images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the data construction pipeline.Source and object-removed videos are globally stylized and filtered, then combined through mask-guided matting to produce foreground- and background-stylized pairs for human verification.

Figure 2:Overview of GRNStyle.(a) Polar style-aware masks bind styles to regions and support multi-region composition.
(b) Anchored mask evidence and geometric support are combined with source features through block-wise gating to guide local video stylization.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison of local video stylization.Examples evaluate stylization inside the editing region, preservation outside it, and temporal consistency.
Foreground and background cases highlight leakage, distortion of preserved content, and boundary inconsistency.
GRNStyle produces localized styles with coherent boundaries and stable non-target content.
Figure 4:Human evaluation results.Values show mean±\pmSD; per-style gains are shown for the ten-style subset.
Figure 5:Mask-conditioning ablation.Representation–geometry conditioning improves spatial localization over the raw encoding.

Figure 6:Data-construction ablation.For curly hair (a) and head contours (b), columns compare direct compositing, removal without matting, and the full pipeline.
Rows show background- and foreground-stylized targets; insets highlight residual silhouettes, clipped contours, and boundary quality.
Figure 7:Representative rejection cases from the data pipeline.
